title: ASA: Our Model of Success
takeaways: ASA = Attitude (how you choose to show up) · Schedule (your calendar, and you showing up, is your office) · Activity (the numbers your planner gives you).
No talent required. Different starts, same three habits.
One agent went 37 days without a sale and kept showing up; another did $50,000 in his first month. Both did ASA.
"If you do ASA in a big way, you will win. I just can't tell you when."

title: Hot Mess Express vs. Perfect Prep
takeaways: Two extremes: the Hot Mess Express (all action, no prep) and Perfect Prep (all prep, no action). Live in the middle.
No amount of preparation prepares you for your first real dial. One hour of practical beats forty hours of conceptual.
Prepared enough = the open plus the five opening objections, cold.
The five: "I don't remember filling that out" · "I already have coverage" · "I don't have time" · "I can't afford it" · "I can't qualify."
Ego in the back seat. We're not doing heart surgery; we're helping Miss Betty protect her family.
Most of your questions are about things you'll only learn by starting. Nobody can tell you what happens after your fifth dial until you've made five.

title: The Winning Day
takeaways: 8:00 ET: virtual office opens (Zoom on).
8:30–9:00 ET, Mon–Sat: Morning Kickoff (Greatest Salesman reading, top-10 goals, coaching).
9:00: dials start (8:00 Central; vets are up early). Go for a sale before lunch.
12:00 on most weekdays: live training (Mon Builder's, Tue Winning System for your first week or two, Thu SRS, Fri Shawn).
2:00 PM, Mon–Fri: Nuts & Bolts. Bring the morning's objections and app snags.
Afternoon into evening: dial block; many clients are home after 5.
Night: a five-minute recap (what worked, where you got stuck), then Goal Card (your 40 points), lock down today's sales, set tomorrow's \#1.
Question mid-block? Write it down, keep dialing, bring it to Nuts & Bolts.
Rules: the 30-second rule, and prime dial hours are for dialing only (recruiting calls go early, at lunch, or after work).

title: The Winning Week
takeaways: Six days a week; Sunday is church and family. Long days early in the week, shorter Friday and Saturday.
Plan the life blocks (date night, the kid's concert) like dial blocks. Planned breaks protect the work blocks.
Before day one: fill out the Wants & Needs / Give Up sheet with your family (or on your own), then walk them through your schedule.

Weekly anchors: Kickoff 8:30 ET Mon–Sat · Mon 12pm Builder's + Monday evening agency sales call · Tue 12pm Winning System (once or twice, to learn leads) · Thu 12pm SRS (IULs and annuities) · Fri 12pm Shawn (the most important call of the week) · Sat New Agent Orientation (new agents).
Compare it to owning a business, not a 40-hour job. Big hours while you're new; you earn your time back.

title: From Your Number to Your Day
takeaways: Number → production → day. Agent Success Plan first, then the Optimum Activity Planner, then the Goal Card (Lesson AC.3).
Worked example: $15K/month take-home ≈ $33K monthly production ≈ 22–27 sales ≈ about 6 a week ≈ one sale a day.
The planner uses your real ratios (dials → contacts → presentations → sales), so you don't need anyone else's.
Your planner sets your daily dial number; 350 dials a day is our floor.
Your why is who this is really for, not "more money."

title: Your Goal Card: 40 Points a Day
takeaways: The Goal Card tracks your day in two-hour blocks. Dials are your base input; they're tracked but earn no points.
Points: Contact 1 · Appointment 2 · Presentation 3 · Sale 5. One person can be worth up to 11 points.
40 points a day is the target, and hitting it consistently is how agents get wildly successful here.
Many ways to 40. Example: 22 contacts + 4 presentations + 1 appointment + 1 sale = 41.
Save the card every night. It compares day, week and month, and with your premium and hours it shows what each dial and hour is worth.
Be your own boss. If you're not tracking, nobody can coach you, and most people overestimate what they did.
Separate yourself from the result. Get your 40 points; the sales follow. Points are the Activity in ASA.

title: Your Call Toolkit: Script Navigator + Product Wizard
takeaways: Script Navigator = your script + client profile. It prompts the follow-ups (e.g., metformin → diabetes? A1C?).
One button pushes the profile into the Product Wizard, which ranks carriers likely to approve, by best fit for the client.
Turn off carriers you aren't contracted with yet.
Quote in the carrier's portal → numbers back into the Navigator → present Maximum Coverage / Recommended / Basic → copy and paste into the app.
Fallback, any time: the soft hold to the dial room's senior underwriter.

title: Start Here: Your Path
takeaways: Your next lesson, A.1, is our model of success: ASA.
Part 1, Clear to Dial: 21 short lessons, required before your first live call.
Part 2, Learn While Dialing: the full library, finished in your first 30 days while you're on the phones.
Don't wait to finish everything before you dial. One hour of practical is worth forty hours of conceptual.
Contracting runs in parallel. Not licensed yet? Finishing your license is job one: application, fingerprints, exam.
I'm asking your permission to hold you to your highest standards.

title: Set Up Your Machine Before Day One
takeaways: Call tools: bookmark the Script Navigator and the Product Wizard (Lesson T.1 shows both).
Carriers: bookmark each agent portal as contracts land and test your login once.
Follow-up stack: Legacy Safeguard account, the client follow-up sequence (Agent Portal → Resources, copy and paste), and thank-you cards sent right away.
Goat CRM comes later, once you're hitting your dial number. Do the hard thing first.
Cheap and ready beats fancy and later.

title: The Winning System
takeaways: Lead types: aged/$1 (where you start), fresh/real-time (higher intent), plus direct mail, telemarketed, Facebook/internet, referrals, and your own warm market.
You manage all your leads in GoatLeads.
Leads are PERISHABLE — work fresh leads fast, triple-dialing across the first 24 hours. Sitting on a lead is money thrown away.
The ramp skeleton: Month 1 — $500/week on aged ($1) leads; Month 2 — $500 aged + $500 fresh; Month 3 — $500 aged + $1,000 fresh → $30K.
Keep scaling by reinvesting while holding comfortable close and show ratios.
Your only two metrics: CPA (cost per acquisition) and what you keep.
It's taught live every Tuesday at 12pm ET. Come once or twice with your numbers; the live call is where current numbers and ratios get worked.

title: Plan Education & Get Your Price
takeaways: Educate by contrast: Accidental only (accidents only) · Term (10–30 years, then it expires; usually for healthy, younger clients) · Whole life (permanent, locked-in, builds value).
For healthy clients, a 4th option: more affordable permanent coverage, your future IUL bridge.
They already have a policy? Never call it bad. "That was a good option when you got it… let's see what's best for you today." Compare, don't criticize.
They write down the five benefits: Permanent · Locked-In Rate · Living Benefits · Tax-Free · Cash Value.
Get the price: Script Navigator → Product Wizard → carrier quote → back into the Navigator.
Or soft-hold to the dial room's senior underwriter. It builds trust.

title: Live Dials & the Release Ladder
takeaways: The live dial room runs all day, every day. It's your classroom and your backup. Join today.
Off mute on live calls: you ask, the room helps. I can't help you if I can't hear you.
You'll hear the closers get told no. Nobody closes everyone.
Coaching comes from your recorded calls: send one or two to your manager or mentor (the open and where it went sideways).

The Release Ladder: (1) Listen · (2) Shadow + take notes (bring your objection tally to 2pm Nuts & Bolts) · (3) Practice: answer each objection in your head as if you were the agent · (4) Supervised calls on your first aged leads · (5) Solo.
The solo gate is behavioral: the full script plus the core objections, unaided. Until then, you dial in the dial room, off mute.

title: Attitude Is a Choice
takeaways: Mindset is what shows up; attitude is what you choose to do with it. You control the next move.
Our attitude: gratitude, optimism, a servant's heart. We know who's in charge.
The quiet voice never says "quit." It says "can you do this forever? Then why does today matter?" Answer it with the next dial.
Attitude is contagious, both ways.

title: It Just Is: Same Event, Different Story
takeaways: A policy falling off is the same event whether it's your 1st or your 10th. Only the story changes. It just is.
"That's lesson \#728." Every lesson is paid for once.
The mirror: not "they got lucky," but "what did they do differently, and what can I do better?"
Comparison is the thief of all joy, and it leads you to make excuses for yourself. Same talent, different skill.
After a hang-up: "Were they my client anyway?" Some will, some won't, so what, next.
Leads come in runs. Live in the middle: nobody should be able to tell from your mood whether you made four sales or none.
Fall in love with the process; detach from the result of any single call (Stan Smith).

title: Would You Last the 37 Days?
takeaways: The dip is normal. Knowing it's coming is how people get through it.
One agent went 37 days without a sale and now leads one of the biggest organizations in the company.
My first 5 months: about $20K total after a 20-year corporate career. First in, last out, and I refused to quit.
The business works: 200 years old, millions underinsured, endless leads. If it isn't working yet, the fix is in you, and you can fix you.
Today's activity shows up in weeks, not hours. "Time either promotes you or exposes you."

title: Preach It, Act It, Become It
thumb: Preach It. Act It. Become It.
takeaways: Preach it: say who you're becoming, out loud, everywhere, starting with yourself. Kickoff goal-writing is preaching.
Act it: show up like it's already true, even in small steps.
Become it: repeated long enough, it's just who you are.
Slumps start when you stop preaching.
Changing a habit? Give it twice as long as you spent on the old one ("double it"). (Stan Smith)

title: The Reverse Reality Check
takeaways: Reverse reality check: dials ÷ hours worked. 100 dials in 10 hours = about 10 minutes of real work per hour.
A no-answer dial takes 5–6 seconds; about 3 dials a minute is realistic.
Do the hard thing first: dial by hand, then add GOAT CRM with auto-dialing once you're hitting your number.
Tools speed up a working process; they don't create one.
The script feels weird because it's new, not because it's wrong. Run it 27 more times.
